newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to examine tax breaks on takeovers.
newsitem.headline: Germany to examine tax breaks on takeovers.

text.p: The German Bundestag lower house of parliament on Thursday called on the government to examine whether tax breaks on the takeover of lossmaking companies should be limited.
Coalition deputies passed resolution attached to Finance Minister Theo Waigel's 1998 tax reform, calling for the government to issue an opinion as soon as possible.

Buying up lossmaking companies and merging them into the new owner is a method used by many German companies to cut their tax exposure, although business groups say that many jobs have been saved thanks to the arrangement.
The Bonn government, meanwhile, is looking for ways to boost revenues to help its bid to qualify for Europe's single currency.

The German business lobby reacted with outrage to changes introduced last week to the 1998 tax bill which would impose limits on tax writeoffs against losses and scrap tax exemptions built up by utilities to shut down nuclear power plants.
